$ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} $

If $y = \ln(2x+1) - \arsech(2x+1),$ then $\dfrac { extrm{d}y}{ extrm{d}x}=$
question.explanation:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arsech x) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}. \]

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get \begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}( \ln(2x+1) - \arsech(2x+1)) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}( \ln(2x+1)) - \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}( \arsech(2x+1)) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{2x+1} - \left( - \dfrac{1}{(2x+1) \sqrt{1 - (2x+1)^2}}\right) \cdot (2x+1)'\\[5pt] & =\dfrac{2}{2x+1} + \dfrac{1}{(2x+1) \sqrt{1 - 4x^2 - 4x - 1}}\cdot 2 \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{2}{2x+1} + \dfrac{2}{(2x+1) \sqrt{- 4x^2 - 4x}} \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{2}{2x+1}\left(1+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{- 4x(x+1)}}\right) \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{2}{2x+1}\left(1+\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{- x(x+1)}}\right) . \end{align*}

$ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} $

If $y = \ln(x-2) + \arcoth(x - 1),$ then $\dfrac { extrm{d}y}{ extrm{d}x}=$
question.explanation:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arcoth x) = \dfrac{1}{1-x^2}. \]

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}( \ln(x-2) + \arcoth(x - 1) ) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}( \ln(x-2) ) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}( \arcoth(x - 1) ) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{x-2} + \dfrac{1}{1 - (x-1)^2} \cdot (x-1)'\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{x-2} + \dfrac{1}{1 - (x^2 - 2x + 1)} \cdot 1\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{x-2} + \dfrac{1}{2x - x^2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{x-2} - \dfrac{1}{x(x - 2)}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{x-2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x} \right)\\[5pt] %& = \dfrac{1}{x-2}\left(\dfrac{x-1}{x} \right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{x-1}{x(x-2)}. \end{align*}

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arsech x) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}. \]

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get \begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} &= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left[\dfrac{1}{4}\arsech\left(x^{4}\right)\right] \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\left[-\dfrac{1}{x^{4}\sqrt{1-\left(x^{4}\right)^2}}\right] \cdot \left(x^{4}\right)' \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{4x^{4}\sqrt{1-x^{8}}}\cdot 4x^{3} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{1-x^{8}}}}. \end{align*}

In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a product $u(x)\cdot v(x)$ with $u(x)=\sin{x}$ and $v(x)=\arcsch{x}.$

Therefore, we apply the product rule as follows: \begin{align} f'(x) &= u'(x)\cdot v(x) + u(x)\cdot v'(x)\\[5pt] &= \left(\sin{x}\right)'\cdot \arcsch{x} + \sin{x}\cdot \left(\arcsch{x}\right)' \\[5pt] &= \cos{x}\cdot \arcsch{x}\;+\; \sin{x}\cdot\left(-\dfrac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}\right) \\[5pt] &= \cos{x}\cdot \arcsch{x} - \dfrac{1}{|x|}\cdot\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray] { \dfrac{\sin{x}}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}} }. \end{align}

question.explanation:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a product $u(x)\cdot v(x)$ with $u(x)=x + 2$ and $v(x)=\arcoth{x}.$

Therefore, we apply the product rule as follows: \begin{align} f'(x) &= u'(x)\cdot v(x) + u(x)\cdot v'(x)\\[5pt] &= \left(x + 2\right)'\cdot \arcoth{x} + (x + 2)\cdot \left(\arcoth{x}\right)' \\[5pt] &= 1\cdot \arcoth{x}\;+\;(x + 2)\cdot\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - x^{2}}\right) \\[5pt] &= \arcoth{x} + \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray] {\dfrac{x + 2}{1 - x^{2}}}. \end{align}
